review_scope: Complete 76-line pinned organization policy article read, including metadata/redirects, headings, cost warning, nested includes, agent-app exception, entitlement and visibility conditions, links and non-candidate context. All 38 parsed candidates separately accounted. Five new reusable fragments read completely; prior paid-plan/navigation fragments re-read without duplicate receipts. No target operation, actual authorization, external linked-page assurance, rights/adoption or independent omission certificate.

claims.statement: Organization policy scope concerns users licensed by that organization on Business/Enterprise plans, not every estate user.
Organization owners are the declared administrators for this policy procedure; documentation role scope is not proof of actual actor authorization.
Organization policy article uses the Copilot cloud feature definition; no GHES version range follows.
The enterprise-override include prevents organization overrides of enterprise-selected policy; exact inherited effective scope must be reviewed.
Organization selection, Settings and Copilot navigation precede policy edits; previously reviewed navigation fragments are reused without duplicate artifact receipts.
The Policies page controls privacy and feature availability, distinct from model selection.
The Models page controls models beyond the basic set; these models may incur extra costs.
Each policy has a dropdown enforcement choice; a selected option is not evidence of effective behavior or authorization to change it.
MCP policy limits are supplied by a separately reviewed note; Copilot policy is not blanket governance for GitHub MCP in third-party hosts.
Third-party agent eligibility is delegated to the previously reviewed all-paid-plans permission fragment; an available UI is not purchased entitlement.
For enterprise-owned organizations, third-party agent settings are visible only after an enterprise administrator enables that capability.
Organization agent apps are not enabled by the third-party coding-agent controls.
Organization agent apps use a separate single agent-apps policy; personal Partner agents placement must not be generalized to organization governance.
The organization procedure lists Anthropic Claude and OpenAI Codex as selectable coding agents; choice alone does not establish actual enablement.
Partner coding agents have the same repository set already enabled for cloud agent, not independent unrestricted repository access.
Partner-agent settings use organization navigation plus the Cloud agent page; nested UI instructions remain source evidence, not executable authorization.
Partner-agent enablement requires a per-third-party-agent toggle; no current setting or native enforcement is observed.
Additional feedback/preview options require Business/Enterprise organization plan and enabling Copilot in GitHub.com.
The included feedback option enables feedback opportunities on selected Copilot features; it is not the AI-training opt-out policy.
The included preview option exposes not-generally-available features with flaws/change/discontinuation caveats; preview enablement is not retention coverage.
Organization default-model and enterprise availability pages are further dependencies, not reviewed through these links.
The supported-surfaces-for-policies page is an independent dependency needed to determine enforcement coverage across products.
